evidence: app/src/index.tsx:77-81 — Abilities route is one contiguous block, plus one import line (index.tsx:7)
app/src/views/details.tsx:53-75 — loadAbility/AbilityPage fully contained in one module; hidden-ability note logic lives here too (details.tsx:56-58)
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:284-293 — the only other link site is the Pokémon page's Abilities section, one removable block
app/public/style.css:275 — .card-note is only used by ability hidden cards; removing Abilities leaves this dead CSS
removability.rationale: Deleting a feature means deleting two cohesive blocks plus one section and one dead CSS rule across three files; nothing is scattered, but it's not a single-directory delete.

evidence: app/src/views/components.tsx:20-25 — all four card lists render through one CardList/spriteUrl path, so a sprite fix lands once on the render side
app/src/data.ts:91-100 — cardsForPokemon discards the Pokémon ID from ref.url and rebuilds the card from species, so a sprite fix needs the Card type + this builder changed
app/src/views/home.tsx:44 — second, independent card builder (species-based), must be kept in sync
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:47-70 — move-table sorting (sortRows/sortValue) is one obvious place for sort bugs
changeability.rationale: Most fixes have one obvious home (render components, sort logic, humanize/typeLabel), but the card view-model is constructed in two places, so card-level fixes are a two-site change rather than one.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:4-47 — fetch + cache isolated behind api()/apiUrl()/apiList(); no view touches fetch or cache internals
app/src/views/components.tsx:1-2 — shared components take plain data props (Card, TypeInfo), no loader knowledge
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:153-159 — MoveTable hardcodes the /moves-table partial URL that the route at app/src/index.tsx:52-66 owns; endpoint renames touch both layers
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:77 — loadMoves(pokemon: any) and other `any` signatures erode the seam between loader and view
coupling.rationale: Layering is real and narrow (api → data → views → routes), and server/client split via htmx attributes is idiomatic; the partial-endpoint URL duplicated between route and component and loose `any` typing are the only tangles.

evidence: app/src/views/components.tsx:3-33 — Section/TypeBadge/CardList/Count are small and stretch to real variation (optional card.types, optional card.note)
app/src/data.ts:91 — cardsForPokemon's note callback already generalizes across move/ability/type pages without flag params
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:122-193 — MoveTable absorbs the level-up column variation internally (isLevelUp) and the sortable-header htmx flow
app/src/views/details.tsx:6-35 vs 78-87 — new resources (Items) follow a copy-adapt loader+page template rather than being derived from a shared abstraction
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions are designed around the app's actual variation points and stretch well; adding Items means patterning, not fighting, the existing code, at the cost of a small copy-adapted loader/page pair.

findings.issue: The Card view-model is built in two independent places (cardsForPokemon for move/ability/type pages, and home.tsx:44 from species), so any card-level change — sprite ID, sorting, a new field — must be replicated in both builders.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardsForPokemon (or a single cardFromSpecies helper) to also build home's cards, so the Card type has exactly one construction site; have it carry the default Pokémon ID instead of discarding it from ref.url.

findings.issue: The /pokemon/:name/moves-table partial endpoint and its query parameters (game, method, sort, dir) are encoded both in the route (index.tsx:52-66) and in the hx-get URLs MoveTable constructs (pokemon.tsx:153-159); renaming or adding a param means editing both layers.
findings.suggestion: Derive the partial URL in one helper (e.g. movesTableUrl(species, params)) used by both the component and, if possible, a Hono route path constant.

findings.issue: Loaders and pages rely on `any` (pokemon: any, move/moves records, details.tsx:57,107), so the seam between data helpers and views is untyped; edits can silently break field access.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API records actually used (Species, Pokemon, Move) and type the loaders' returns; the existing Awaited<ReturnType<...>> view typing already shows the pattern.

findings.issue: pokemon.tsx bundles three concerns — Pokémon page, moves data loading (loadMoves/versionGroups), and the sortable MoveTable component — making the file the natural dumping ground for the next Pokémon-related change.
findings.suggestion: Split into views/pokemon.tsx and views/moves.tsx (loader + table) if the file grows further; today the mix is still navigable.

findings.issue: .card-note is styled for a feature-specific detail (ability hidden note) that would become dead CSS if Abilities is removed; other such pairings are fine but this one is the only orphan risk found.
findings.suggestion: None needed now; when removing a feature, grep for its component classes before considering the removal done.

findings.issue: The typecheck script exists but is not wired into build or any test script, so refactorings are only verified by the repo-level acceptance tests.
findings.suggestion: Run tsc --noEmit as part of `npm run build` (or add a pretest hook) so type regressions surface on every change.

summary: A compact, well-layered Hono + htmx app where loaders live next to their views and shared components are small and props-driven, so most changes land in one obvious place. The main editability tax is the duplicated card view-model construction (data.ts vs home.tsx) and the partial-endpoint URL known by both route and component. It's the kind of code you'd extend confidently; the scores reflect small, fixable seams rather than structural problems.
